Wrenfield Toys Brings the Toy Shelf Home
By Paul Andersen, Staff Writer
Every month, dozens of families in Dunham open their doors to a box of toys chosen for their children. The boxes come from Wrenfield Toys, a small shop on Ferrier Street that lets families borrow toys instead of buying them.
Parents choose an age group, and each month a driver drops off a new box and picks up the old one. Plans start at $22 a month. Since launching the service in 2019, owner Teresa Vukovic has hired two part-time drivers, and much of the shop's growth now comes from rentals. Deliveries now reach Dunham and nearby Hadley, and she hopes to add Marston next year.
Ms. Vukovic opened the shop in 2011, and it remains her only location. Customers still visit to browse and to attend regular events. The shop holds reading afternoons for young children every month, runs a winter toy collection for families in need, and offers free repair sessions for broken toys. The next reading afternoon is set for the end of this month.
Details are available at www.wrenfieldtoys.com.

Adopt-a-Bed Program
This spring, the Ferndale Parks Office is launching a program through which residents can help keep the city's public parks attractive. Each volunteer will be responsible for one small flower bed in a neighborhood park from April through September. --[1]--.
Because the beds must stay in good condition all season, volunteers should visit their assigned bed at least once a week to water the plants, remove weeds, and cut off any flowers that have died. When the season ends in late September, they will also clear the bed for winter. --[2]--.
At the start of the season, our staff will hold a short session at each park to show how the beds should be cared for. The office supplies all plants, and each volunteer receives a starter kit containing gloves, a watering can, and hand tools. --[3]--.
Participation is limited to Ferndale residents. Those wishing to reserve a bed should complete the request form at the bottom of this page, indicating the park closest to their home. I coordinate staff training at Norwell Logistics and am planning a two-day retreat for our regional managers. A colleague recommended your hotel to me.
We expect eighteen participants on November 13 and 14. We will need a private meeting room, vegetarian choices at every meal, and parking, since most of the group will drive.

Alma Pereira
Norwell Logistics

Garden Room Package

Screen and projector
Coffee breaks

Terrace Package
